apiRateBurst.description: How many requests may go out at once above the rate. Defaults to twice the rate, at least 10, when set to 0.

apiRateLimit.description: The most requests per second. Defaults to 8, and 0 turns the limit off.

apiRetryMax.description: How many times a failed request is retried. Defaults to 4.

apiRetryWaitMax.description: The longest wait before a retry, in seconds, also when Better Stack asks to wait longer. Defaults to 300.

apiRetryWaitMin.description: The shortest wait before a retry, in seconds. Defaults to 10.

apiTimeout.description: How long one request may take, in seconds. Defaults to 60, and 0 turns the timeout off.

apiToken.description: Better Stack API token. Falls back to the BETTERSTACK_API_TOKEN environment variable.

endpoint.description: The API base URL to use instead of Better Stack's, such as a test server.

teamId.description: Selects the team when the API token can reach several.

alertType.description: The type of the condition, 'threshold' or 'relative'.

operator.description: The comparison the condition makes, from the same values as `operator`.

seriesNames.description: The series the condition is limited to. An empty list means every series.

seriesNamesExcept.description: The series the condition ignores while it watches every other series.

stringValue.description: Threshold value for a string series. null when the condition compares `value`.

value.description: Threshold value. null when the condition compares `stringValue`.

teamId.description: Team ID, such as 't123'.

teamName.description: Team name.

name.description: The name of a variable on the alert's dashboard or exploration.

selectedLabel.description: For a 'select_predefined_sql' variable, the label of the filter the alert uses.

values.description: The values the alert uses for the variable, as strings.

accessKeyId.description: The access key ID Better Stack uses to write to the bucket.

endpoint.description: The S3-compatible endpoint URL of the bucket. It can't be changed after the bucket is set.

keepDataAfterRetention.description: Whether data stays in the bucket after the retention period. It can't be changed after the bucket is set.

name.description: The bucket's name, which Better Stack reads from `endpoint`.

secretAccessKey.description: The secret access key for `accessKeyId`. It's write-only.

acceptIncomingSessions.description: Continue sessions that arrive from your other domains.

collect.description: The features the JavaScript tag collects, each on or off.

customConfig.description: JavaScript code the tag runs when it loads.

decorateForms.description: Also share sessions through forms that submit to your other domains.

eventsBatchIntervalSeconds.description: Seconds between batches of events, at least 2.

excludeSelectors.description: CSS selectors of elements excluded from session replays and autocapture.

maskSelectors.description: CSS selectors of elements whose text session replays mask.

ownDomain.description: Your own subdomain to serve the tag from. Its CNAME record must point to `proxy.betterstack.net`.

sampling.description: Sampling rates of the JavaScript tag, as percentages.

sessionTimeoutMinutes.description: Session timeout in minutes, from 1 to 60.

sharedSessionDomains.description: Your other domains to share sessions with.

memory.description: Record JavaScript heap memory, in Chrome only.

errors.description: Percentage of errors sent, from 0 to 100.

replays.description: Percentage of sessions recorded as session replays, from 0 to 100.

webEvents.description: Percentage of sessions that send web events, from 0 to 100.

appFilter.description: The condition that keeps only the application's rows in its parent's raw collections. null unless the application is connected to a source.

database.description: The ClickHouse database that holds the application's data.

metricsAppFilter.description: The condition that keeps only the application's rows in its parent's metrics collection. null unless the application is connected to a source.

recent.description: The collection of the last 30 minutes for each row type the application holds, keyed by row type, such as 'exceptions' or 'metrics'.

s3.description: The collection that holds older rows of every type.

attribute.description: The catalog attribute to set, by id or name. Responses include both.

values.description: Values to set for this attribute.

id.description: The catalog attribute's ID.

name.description: The catalog attribute's name.

email.description: Referenced user's e-mail, returned for a User. A user can also be found by e-mail.

itemId.description: ID of the referenced item. For a user it's 'u123' or their e-mail. For a team it's 't123', and for any other item it's the item's own ID. Responses return users and teams in this form. Get a user's ID via [List team members](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/team-members/list/), and a team's ID via [List teams](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/teams/list/). A reference needs one of `itemId`, `name` or `email`.

name.description: Referenced item's name, or null when the item has no name or no longer exists. An item can also be found by its name instead of `itemId`. A monitor, a Slack integration and a Zapier Zap can't be looked up by name.

type.description: `String`, or the type of the referenced item, which is one of User, Team, EscalationPolicy, OnCallSchedule, Monitor, SlackIntegration, LinearIntegration, JiraIntegration, MicrosoftTeamsIntegration, ZapierZap, OutgoingWebhook, PagerDutyIntegration or Source. Required except for `{value}`.

value.description: The text of a String value. Required when `type` is `String`.

id.description: ID of an existing attribute to keep. Leave it out to keep the attribute with the same name, or to add a new one.

name.description: Attribute name. Names must be unique within the relation.

position.description: Display order, set by the order of the list. Primary attributes count from 0 and added attributes from 1000.

primary.description: Whether records are matched by this attribute. Defaults to false.

bufferMaxEvents.description: How many events the collector's memory buffer holds before it moves them to disk. Defaults to 10000.

components.description: Which components the collector runs, each true or false.

diskBatchSizeMb.description: Batching on disk, the size of the collector's disk buffer in MB. Defaults to 3000, and it can't be less than 256.

logLineLengthLimitKb.description: Maximum log line length in kB, from 4 to 128. Longer lines are dropped. Defaults to 8.

logsSampleRate.description: Percentage of logs to keep, from 0 to 100. Defaults to 100.

memoryBatchSizeMb.description: Batching in memory, how much data the collector batches before sending it, in MB. Defaults to 20.

mergeLogs.description: Whether the collector merges lines that continue a log entry, such as a stack trace, into the entry before them.

mergeLogsConfig.description: The VRL condition `mergeLogs` uses to tell whether a line starts a new log entry. Any other line joins the entry before it.

namespacesOptions.description: Options per namespace, keyed by namespace name. A map replaces the stored one, and an empty map clears it.

servicesOptions.description: Options per service, keyed by service name. A map replaces the stored one, and an empty map clears it.

tracesSampleRate.description: Percentage of traces to keep, from 0 to 100. Defaults to 100, and 0 drops every trace.

whenFull.description: What the collector does when its disk buffer is full, 'drop_newest' to drop new events or 'block' to wait until there's room.

ebpfRedMetrics.description: Service map and request rate, error and duration metrics with eBPF.

logsDocker.description: Collect logs of Docker containers that use the default json-file logging driver.

logsHost.description: Collect logs from the host's /var/log directory.

logsKubernetes.description: Collect Kubernetes container logs and events.

metricsCluster.description: Collect Kubernetes object state metrics, such as pods, workloads, nodes and volumes.

metricsDatabases.description: Former name of `metricsCluster`. It reads back as `metricsCluster` does. Write `metricsCluster` instead.

metricsHostOs.description: Collect CPU, memory, disk, filesystem and network metrics of the host.

metricsOtherDatabases.description: Collect Redis, MongoDB, Memcached and Kafka metrics.

metricsProcessStatistics.description: Collect the host's process and thread counts. It can use significant CPU on a host that runs very many processes.

tracesOpentelemetry.description: Accept OpenTelemetry traces from your SDKs over OTLP.

ingestTraces.description: Whether to ingest the namespace's traces.

logSampling.description: Percentage of the namespace's logs to keep, from 0 to 100.

ingestTraces.description: Whether to ingest the service's traces.

logSampling.description: Percentage of the service's logs to keep, from 0 to 100.

accessKeyId.description: The access key ID Better Stack uses to write to the bucket.

endpoint.description: The S3-compatible endpoint URL of the bucket. It can't be changed after the bucket is set.

keepDataAfterRetention.description: Whether data stays in the bucket after the retention period. It can't be changed after the bucket is set.

name.description: The bucket's name, which Better Stack reads from `endpoint`.

secretAccessKey.description: The secret access key for `accessKeyId`. Write-only, so it's never returned.

nameKey.description: The field to extract the service name from, such as `service.name`.

typeKey.description: The field to extract the service's platform from, such as `service.type`. Better Stack matches platforms like Nginx, PostgreSQL or Redis in its value.

host.description: Host to connect to the cluster on.

name.description: The cluster's name.

email.description: The creator's e-mail.

id.description: The creator's user ID, such as 'u123'.

connectionUrl.description: The URL to connect to for this source's data.

dataSources.description: ClickHouse collection names you can query for this source.

sourceId.description: The source's ID.

teamName.description: The name of the team the source belongs to.

coordinates.description: Coordinate blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query, as an empty list when there are none. Read-only.

filters.description: Filter blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Left out when not set. Read-only.

funnelQuery.description: Funnel definition of a `funnelQuery` query, with the session field, the steps, each a name and its conditions, and an optional breakdown. Read-only.

groupBy.description: Grouping blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Left out when not set. Read-only.

having.description: Having blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query, as an empty list when there are none. Read-only.

id.description: The query's ID.

name.description: The query's name. Left out when the query has none.

orderBy.description: Ordering blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query, as an empty list when there are none. Read-only.

pointSize.description: Point size blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Left out when not set. Read-only.

pqlQuery.description: PQL source of a 'pql_expression' query. Read-only.

queryType.description: The query's type. You can write 'sql_expression', 'tail_query' and `staticText` queries. The types the editor builds are read-only. They're 'pql_expression', 'query_builder', 'tail_query_builder', `funnelQuery`, 'promql_query', 'promql_v2_query' and 'promql_via_llm'.

sourceVariable.description: The sources the query reads, as the name of a 'source' variable, such as 'source', or a `source:` reference to specific sources. Defaults to 'source'.

sqlQuery.description: The SQL the query runs. Returned for 'sql_expression', 'pql_expression', 'query_builder', 'tail_query_builder' and `funnelQuery` queries.

staticText.description: The Markdown text a `staticText` query shows. Left out when not set.

where.description: Where blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query, as an empty list when there are none. Read-only.

whereCondition.description: The filter of a 'tail_query' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Left out when not set.

xAxes.description: X-axis blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query, as an empty list when there are none. Read-only.

yAxes.description: Y-axis blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Left out when not set. Read-only.

conditionValue.description: The value a filter block compares against.

direction.description: The sort direction of an order block, 'asc' or 'desc'.

exploreBlockType.description: What the block reads, such as 'count', 'field', 'json_value', 'json_value_from_column', 'special_column', 'virtual_field' or 'search'.

intervalSeconds.description: The time bucket size in seconds, for a time block on the X axis.

kind.description: 'metric' for an aggregated value, or `label` for a raw dimension.

logicalOperator.description: How a filter block joins the filters before it, 'and' or 'or'. Defaults to 'and'.

measure.description: The aggregation applied to the value, such as 'avg', 'count', 'uniq', `max`, `min`, 'sum' or 'p95'.

name.description: The name the block is shown with. The editor shows `value` when it's empty.

operator.description: The comparison of a filter block.

operatorSymbol.description: The filter block's comparison written as a symbol.

seriesName.description: The name a Y-axis or coordinates block's series is shown as.

type.description: The value's data type, such as 'datetime'.

value.description: The column or field the block reads, such as 'dt'.

valueType.description: 'rate' to chart the value's rate of change.

colorGreenWords.description: Values a number chart shows in green, separated by commas.

colorLowerThreshold.description: Lower threshold of a number chart's colors.

colorMode.description: How a number chart colors its value. Usually 'auto', 'high_green', 'high_red' or 'specific_words'.

colorRedWords.description: Values a number chart shows in red, separated by commas.

colorUpperThreshold.description: Upper threshold of a number chart's colors.

colorYellowWords.description: Values a number chart shows in yellow, separated by commas.

columnUnits.description: Unit of each table column, by column name.

columnWidths.description: Width of each table column, by column name, as the chart editor saves it.

customUnit.description: Whether `unit` is your own suffix, shown after the value as written and never scaled.

filteredSeries.description: Series the chart shows, by name.

forceSourceSeries.description: Whether the chart shows one series per source.

fresh.description: Whether the chart skips cached results.

funnelUnitName.description: Word a funnel chart counts in, such as 'people'.

groupByColumns.description: Up to two columns a hierarchy chart groups its hexagons by.

guessedSeriesColors.description: Colors the chart picked for its series, keyed by `seriesName`.

heatmapColorMode.description: How a heatmap colors its cells. Usually 'gradient' or 'categorized'.

label.description: A legend placement the chart editor saves next to `legend`, such as 'shown_below'. Charts ignore it and place the legend by `legend`.

labelColumn.description: Column that names each hexagon on a hierarchy chart.

legend.description: Where the legend is shown. Usually 'hidden', 'shown_below', 'shown_below_with_statistics' or 'shown_right'.

linkTemplate.description: Link a hierarchy chart opens when you click a hexagon, with `{{column}}` placeholders.

locationColumn.description: Column holding the location on a map chart.

locationLabel.description: What a map chart's tooltip names, either the closest city or country or the value as sent. Usually 'automatic' or 'original_value'.

max.description: Upper bound of a gauge, the goal value.

maxValue.description: Highest value of a hierarchy chart's color scale.

minValue.description: Lowest value of a hierarchy chart's color scale.

orientation.description: Direction of the bars on a bar chart. Usually 'vertical' or 'horizontal'.

palette.description: Color scale of a hierarchy chart. Usually 'green_to_red' or 'red_to_green'.

percentageHighlightColumns.description: Table columns holding ratios from 0 to 1, shown with a bar.

pointSizeColumn.description: Column that sets each point's size on a scatter chart.

projection.description: Map projection of a map chart, such as 'mercator'.

publishedCacheFor.description: Seconds a published chart's results are cached, 3 by default.

publishedFormat.description: Format a published chart is served in, 'json' by default.

rowTemplates.description: Live tail row format of each source, by source ID.

sampling.description: Percentage of data the chart samples.

seriesColors.description: Color of each series, keyed by its `seriesName`, as a hex color such as `#22c55e`.

seriesColumn.description: Column that splits the data into series. On a heatmap it's the Y axis column.

seriesCustomUnit.description: Whether `seriesUnit` is your own suffix.

seriesOrder.description: Order the series are shown in, by name.

seriesUnit.description: Unit of a heatmap's Y axis labels.

showPreviousPeriod.description: Whether a line chart also shows the previous period.

stacking.description: How series are stacked. Usually 'dont_stack', 'stack' or 'stack_to_100'.

tableWidth.description: Width of the table the `columnWidths` were saved for.

text.description: Markdown text of a text chart.

timeColumn.description: Column on the X axis, 'time' by default. For a category bar chart it's the grouping column.

treatMissingValues.description: How gaps in the data are drawn. Usually 'connected', 'disconnected', 'zero' or 'previous'.

treatZeroValues.description: How zero values are drawn, 'keep' or 'drop_disconnected'. Defaults to 'keep'.

unit.description: Unit the values are shown in, such as 'percent', 'bytes' or 'ms'. Table charts use `columnUnits` instead.

valueCategories.description: Label and color of each cell value of a categorized heatmap.

valueColumns.description: Result columns that hold the values to chart.

xAxisAnnotations.description: Vertical lines drawn at values on the X axis, each with a label and color. A value is a time or a number, as the X axis reads it.

xAxisType.description: How the X axis is read. Usually 'time', `value` or 'category'.

yAxisAnnotations.description: Horizontal lines drawn at values on the Y axis, each with a label and color.

yAxisAutoRange.description: How a line chart fits its Y axis when no bounds are set. Usually 'include_zero' or 'fit_data'.

yAxisMax.description: Highest value on the Y axis.

yAxisMin.description: Lowest value on the Y axis.

yAxisScale.description: Scale of the Y axis. Usually 'linear' or 'log'.

yAxisType.description: How the Y axis of a scatter chart is read. Usually `value` or 'category'.

customUnit.description: Whether `unit` is your own suffix, shown after the value as written and never scaled.

actionType.description: What the step does. Required on 'resolve_remove' steps, which accept only resolving or removing. On branching steps it applies when the incident matches. It defaults to running another policy when you set `escalationPolicyId` or `policyMetadataKey`, and to stopping otherwise. 'escalate_to_policy': Runs the escalation policy in `escalationPolicyId` or `policyMetadataKey` and stops this policy. 'resolve_incident': Resolves the incident and stops this policy. 'remove_incident': Removes the incident for good and stops this policy. 'do_not_escalate': Stops this policy.

days.description: The days on which the time window applies, out of 'mon', 'tue', 'wed', 'thu', 'fri', 'sat' and 'sun'. Used on 'time_branching' steps and defaults to every day.

escalationPolicyId.description: The ID of another escalation policy in your organization to run when the incident matches. Used on 'time_branching' and 'metadata_branching' steps. Can't be combined with `policyMetadataKey`.

instructionsComment.description: The instructions posted as a comment into the incident timeline. Supports Markdown, checkboxes like `- [ ] Step 1`, and values from the incident's metadata as `{key}`, such as `{server_region}`. Required on 'instructions' steps.

instructionsReminderEnabled.description: Whether to post a reminder periodically until every checkbox in the instructions is checked. Defaults to false.

instructionsReminderIntervalHours.description: How often the reminder is posted, in hours, on 'instructions' steps with `instructionsReminderEnabled` on. At least '1', and '4' by default.

metadataKey.description: The incident metadata key the step checks. Required on 'metadata_branching' steps.

metadataValues.description: The metadata values that match, at least one. Required on 'metadata_branching' steps. Each is `{type: "String", value}`, `{type: 'no_value'}` or a catalog item reference. 'no_value' matches when the key is missing or blank.

policyMetadataKey.description: A key in the incident's metadata that holds the escalation policy to run when the incident matches, instead of `escalationPolicyId`. Used on 'time_branching' and 'metadata_branching' steps. If the key is missing or holds no policy, the policy stops.

severityId.description: The ID of the severity that sets how the step's members are notified. Required on 'escalation' steps. Get the severity ID via [List severities](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/list-all-severities/).

stepMembers.description: Who or what the step notifies, at least one member. Required on 'escalation' steps. Each member has a `type`, plus an `id`, `email` or `metadataKey` depending on the type.

timeFrom.description: Start of the time window, in `HH:MM` format. Required on 'time_branching' steps.

timeTo.description: End of the time window, in `HH:MM` format. Required on 'time_branching' steps.

timezone.description: The time zone of the time window. Required on 'time_branching' steps.

type.description: The step type. 'escalation': Notifies people or integrations. 'time_branching': Acts when the incident happens in a time window, and otherwise continues with the next step. 'metadata_branching': Acts when the incident's metadata matches a value, and otherwise continues with the next step. 'instructions': Posts instructions into the incident timeline. 'resolve_remove': Resolves or removes the incident.

waitBefore.description: How long the step waits after the previous step, in seconds, from '0' to '691200', which is 8 days. Defaults to '0'. Leave it out when the step waits until a time of day with `waitUntilTime`.

waitUntilDays.description: The days on which `waitUntilTime` applies, out of 'mon', 'tue', 'wed', 'thu', 'fri', 'sat' and 'sun'. Defaults to every day.

waitUntilTime.description: The time of day the step runs, in `HH:MM` format, instead of waiting `waitBefore`. Requires `waitUntilTimezone`. Responses show it in place of `waitBefore` on such steps.

waitUntilTimezone.description: The time zone of `waitUntilTime`, as a Rails time zone name such as `London` or `Eastern Time (US & Canada)`.

email.description: A User item's e-mail, returned for a User. A user can also be found by e-mail.

itemId.description: The catalog item's ID. For a user it's 'u123' or their e-mail. For a team it's 't123', and for any other item it's the item's own ID. Responses return users and teams in this form. Get a user's ID via [List team members](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/team-members/list/), and a team's ID via [List teams](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/teams/list/).

name.description: The catalog item's name. An item can also be found by its name instead of `itemId`.

type.description: `String`, 'no_value', or a catalog item's type, which is one of `User`, `Team`, `EscalationPolicy`, `OnCallSchedule`, `Monitor`, `SlackIntegration`, `LinearIntegration`, `JiraIntegration`, `MicrosoftTeamsIntegration`, `ZapierZap`, `OutgoingWebhook`, `PagerDutyIntegration` or `Source`. 'no_value' matches when the incident's metadata doesn't have the key or the key is empty.

value.description: The text of a `String` value.

email.description: The e-mail of a 'user' member, instead of its id.

id.description: The ID of the member's target. Required for 'user' unless `email` is set, and for 'policy', 'ai_sre' and every type that notifies one integration. A 'user' member is 'u123' or their e-mail, and responses return 'u123'. A 'current_on_call' member accepts an on-call calendar to notify instead of the team's default. An 'entire_team' member accepts another team in the organization, as its ID such as 't123'. Responses return it the same way. Both come back without an ID when they use the policy's own team. Get a user's ID via [List team members](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/team-members/list/), and a team's ID via [List teams](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/teams/list/).

metadataKey.description: The incident metadata key whose stored users, teams, on-call calendars, escalation policies and integrations an 'incident_metadata' member notifies.

type.description: The member type. 'current_on_call' notifies whoever is on call, and 'entire_team' everyone in the team. 'user' notifies one person, 'policy' runs another escalation policy, 'incident_metadata' notifies what the incident's metadata stores under `metadataKey`, and 'ai_sre' starts an AI SRE investigation. A member can also be one integration, with type 'webhook', 'email_integration', 'slack_integration', 'linear_integration', 'jira_integration', 'halo_psa_integration', 'microsoft_teams_integration', 'pagerduty_integration', 'zapier_webhook', 'zoom_integration' or 'google_meet_integration'. Or it can be every integration of one kind, with type 'all_slack_integrations', 'all_linear_integrations', 'all_jira_integrations', 'all_microsoft_teams_integrations', 'all_zapier_integrations', 'all_pagerduty_integrations', 'all_webhook_integrations', 'all_email_integrations', 'all_splunk_on_call_integrations', 'all_incident_io_integrations', 'all_zoom_integrations' or 'all_google_meet_integrations'.

'table_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' queries. 'bar_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' and 'tail_query' queries. 'number_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' and 'tail_query' queries. 'heatmap_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' queries. 'anomalies_chart': Accepts 'tail_query' queries. 'pie_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' queries. 'scatter_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' queries. 'gauge_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' and 'tail_query' queries. 'tail_chart': Accepts 'tail_query' queries. 'static_text_chart': Accepts a `staticText` query. allowMultipleValues.description: Whether a 'select_value' or 'select_with_sql' variable accepts more than one value at a time.

defaultValues.description: The variable's default values as strings, or an empty array when it has none.

filters.description: The saved filters of a 'select_predefined_sql' variable. Each has a `label` and an `sql` query, a complete query that returns one column with the filter's options.

name.description: The variable's name, used as `{{name}}` in queries.

selectedLabel.description: The label of the selected filter of a 'select_predefined_sql' variable. When not sent, the first filter is selected. A label that matches none of `filters` is refused.

sourceIds.description: The IDs of the sources a 'source' variable selects. They set the selection. Each must be a source the team can access.

sqlDefinition.description: The SQL expression whose distinct values are the options of a 'select_with_sql' variable, such as `JSONExtractString(raw, 'service')`. It runs against the variable's source over the selected range.

structuredValue.description: The variable's other settings, such as the selected sources of a 'source' variable in `canonicalSourceIds` and its services in `serviceIds`, or the saved filters of a 'select_predefined_sql' variable. Left out when not set.

values.description: The variable's current values as strings, or an empty array when it has none. For a 'source' variable, these are the IDs of the selected sources.

label.description: The filter's label, shown in the variable's menu.

sql.description: A complete query that returns one column with the filter's options.

canonicalSourceIds.description: Selected sources of a 'source' variable. Source IDs in `values` set them.

filters.description: Saved filters, each a label and the SQL that lists its values.

label.description: The filter's label, shown in the variable's menu.

sql.description: A complete query that returns one column with the filter's options.

email.description: Referenced user's e-mail, returned for a User. A user can also be found by e-mail.

itemId.description: ID of the referenced item. For a user it's 'u123' or their e-mail. For a team it's 't123', and for any other item it's the item's own ID. Responses return users and teams in this form. Get a user's ID via [List team members](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/team-members/list/), and a team's ID via [List teams](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/teams/list/).

name.description: Referenced item's name, or null when the item has no name or no longer exists. An item can also be found by its name instead of `itemId`.

type.description: `String`, or the type of the referenced item, which is one of `User`, `Team`, `EscalationPolicy`, `OnCallSchedule`, `Monitor`, `SlackIntegration`, `LinearIntegration`, `JiraIntegration`, `MicrosoftTeamsIntegration`, `ZapierZap`, `OutgoingWebhook`, `PagerDutyIntegration` or `Source`.

value.description: The text of a `String` value.

content.description: The text to extract around for 'match_before' and 'match_after', or the regular expression for 'match_regex'. Required for those three.

contentAfter.description: Where extraction stops for 'match_between'. Leave it empty to extract to the end.

fieldTarget.description: Which part of the notification to read. 'query_string': The query string of AWS's own HTTPS request, which never contains your message. 'header': A header of AWS's own HTTPS request, which never contains your message. 'body': The message your publisher sent, as plain text. 'json': A value in the message your publisher sent, read as JSON. 'xml': An element in the message your publisher sent, read as XML. 'sns_envelope': A value of the SNS envelope, such as its `Subject`.

matchType.description: What to extract. 'match_before': Extracts the text before `content`. 'match_after': Extracts the text after `content`. 'match_between': Extracts the text between `contentBefore` and `contentAfter`. 'match_regex': Extracts the match of the regular expression in `content`, or its capture group. 'match_everything': Extracts the whole value.

name.description: The metadata key a custom field's value is saved under. Custom fields require it, and it must be unique within its list. Not used by the cause, title and alert ID fields.

specialType.description: The built-in role of this field. null for a custom field. 'alert_id': Extracts the alert ID that ties later notifications to the same incident. 'cause': Extracts the incident cause. 'title': Extracts the incident title.

targetField.description: Which value to read. It's a dot-separated path such as `alert.id` for 'json' and 'query_string', a header name for 'header', a CSS selector for 'xml', or `TopicArn`, `MessageId` or `Subject` for 'sns_envelope'. Not used with 'body'.

content.description: The value to compare with. Must be a valid regular expression for 'matches_regex' and 'matches_regex_not'.

matchType.description: How to compare the value with `content`. 'contains': Matches when the value contains `content`. 'contains_not': Matches when the value doesn't contain `content`. 'matches_regex': Matches when the value matches the regular expression in `content`. 'matches_regex_not': Matches when the value doesn't match the regular expression in `content`. 'equals': Matches when the value equals `content`. 'equals_not': Matches when the value doesn't equal `content`.

subject.description: The e-mail subject, up to 500 characters. Supports incident variables such as `$NAME`, `$STATUS`, `$CAUSE` and `$INCIDENT_URL`, a metadata value as `$METADATA.Key`, all metadata as `$METADATA_ARRAY` and a recipient's attributes as `$RECIPIENT.<key>`. null uses the default template.

title.description: The e-mail title, up to 500 characters. Supports the same variables as `subject`. null uses the default template.

bodyTemplate.description: Request body template, as text. It can use the [metadata variables](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/webhooks/#metadata-variables).

headersTemplate.description: Custom request headers, as a list of objects with `name` and `value`. Header values are sent as written, without template variables.

httpMethod.description: The HTTP method of the request, 'post' by default. A GET request is sent without a body. Valid values: 'head', 'get', 'post', 'put', 'patch', 'options'.

authPassword.description: The password for basic authentication. Set both username and password, or neither.

authUsername.description: The username for basic authentication. Set both username and password, or neither.

bodyTemplate.description: Request body template, as text or as a JSON object. Reads return it as text. An 'incident_change' template can use `$INCIDENT_ID`, `$INCIDENT_URL`, `$NAME`, `$STATUS`, `$CAUSE`, `$URL`, `$HTTP_METHOD`, `$MONITOR_ID`, `$RESOURCE_ID`, `$RESOURCE_TYPE`, `$TEAM_ID`, `$TEAM_NAME`, `$INCIDENT_GROUP_ID`, `$REQUESTER`, `$STARTED_AT`, `$ACKNOWLEDGED_AT`, `$ACKNOWLEDGED_BY`, `$RESOLVED_AT`, `$RESOLVED_BY`, `$RESPONSE_URL`, `$RESPONSE_CONTENT`, `$RESPONSE_OPTIONS`, `$SCREENSHOT_URL`, `$INTEGRATION_IMAGE_URL`, `$REGIONS`, `$ESCALATION_POLICY_ID`, `$CALL`, `$SMS`, `$EMAIL`, `$PUSH`, `$CRITICAL_ALERT`, `$INTEGRATION_ALERT_ID`, `$PLAYWRIGHT_SUMMARY`, `$COMMENT_ID`, `$COMMENT_CONTENT`, `$COMMENT_CREATED_AT`, `$COMMENT_AUTHOR_NAME` and `$COMMENT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`. A 'monitor_change' template can use `$MONITOR_ID`, `$PRONOUNCEABLE_NAME`, `$URL`, `$MONITOR_TYPE`, `$STATUS`, `$MONITOR_GROUP_ID`, `$ESCALATION_POLICY_ID`, `$EXPIRATION_ESCALATION_POLICY_ID`, `$LAST_CHECKED_AT`, `$REQUIRED_KEYWORD`, `$VERIFY_SSL`, `$CHECK_FREQUENCY`, `$CALL`, `$SMS`, `$EMAIL`, `$PUSH`, `$CRITICAL_ALERT`, `$TEAM_WAIT`, `$HTTP_METHOD`, `$REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, `$RECOVERY_PERIOD`, `$REQUEST_BODY`, `$PAUSED_AT`, `$SSL_EXPIRATION`, `$DOMAIN_EXPIRATION`, `$REGIONS` and `$PORT`. An 'on_call_change' template can use `$MESSAGE`, `$EMAILS`, `$EMAILS_JSON_ARRAY`, `$ON_HOLIDAY_EMAILS`, `$ON_HOLIDAY_EMAILS_JSON_ARRAY`, `$CHANGE`, `$ON_CALL_CALENDAR_ID`, `$ON_CALL_CALENDAR_NAME` and `$DEFAULT_ON_CALL_CALENDAR`. Incident and monitor templates can also use the [metadata variables](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/webhooks/#metadata-variables). actionType.description: What the step does. Required on 'resolve_remove' steps, which accept only resolving or removing. On branching steps it applies when the incident matches. It defaults to running another policy when you set `escalationPolicyId` or `policyMetadataKey`, and to stopping otherwise. 'escalate_to_policy': Runs the escalation policy in `escalationPolicyId` or `policyMetadataKey` and stops this policy. 'resolve_incident': Resolves the incident and stops this policy. 'remove_incident': Removes the incident for good and stops this policy. 'do_not_escalate': Stops this policy.

days.description: The days on which the time window applies, out of 'mon', 'tue', 'wed', 'thu', 'fri', 'sat' and 'sun'. Used on 'time_branching' steps and defaults to every day.

escalationPolicyId.description: The ID of another escalation policy in your organization to run when the incident matches. Used on 'time_branching' and 'metadata_branching' steps. Can't be combined with `policyMetadataKey`.

instructionsComment.description: The instructions posted as a comment into the incident timeline. Supports Markdown, checkboxes like `- [ ] Step 1`, and values from the incident's metadata as `{key}`, such as `{server_region}`. Required on 'instructions' steps.

instructionsReminderEnabled.description: Whether to post a reminder periodically until every checkbox in the instructions is checked. Defaults to false.

instructionsReminderIntervalHours.description: How often the reminder is posted, in hours, on 'instructions' steps with `instructionsReminderEnabled` on. At least '1', and '4' by default.

metadataKey.description: The incident metadata key the step checks. Required on 'metadata_branching' steps.

metadataValues.description: The metadata values that match, at least one. Required on 'metadata_branching' steps. Each is `{type: "String", value}`, `{type: 'no_value'}` or a catalog item reference. 'no_value' matches when the key is missing or blank.

policyMetadataKey.description: A key in the incident's metadata that holds the escalation policy to run when the incident matches, instead of `escalationPolicyId`. Used on 'time_branching' and 'metadata_branching' steps. If the key is missing or holds no policy, the policy stops.

severityId.description: The ID of the severity that sets how the step's members are notified. Required on 'escalation' steps. Get the severity ID via [List severities](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/list-all-severities/).

stepMembers.description: Who or what the step notifies, at least one member. Required on 'escalation' steps. Each member has a `type`, plus an `id`, `email` or `metadataKey` depending on the type.

timeFrom.description: Start of the time window, in `HH:MM` format. Required on 'time_branching' steps.

timeTo.description: End of the time window, in `HH:MM` format. Required on 'time_branching' steps.

timezone.description: The time zone of the time window. Required on 'time_branching' steps.

type.description: The step type. 'escalation': Notifies people or integrations. 'time_branching': Acts when the incident happens in a time window, and otherwise continues with the next step. 'metadata_branching': Acts when the incident's metadata matches a value, and otherwise continues with the next step. 'instructions': Posts instructions into the incident timeline. 'resolve_remove': Resolves or removes the incident.

waitBefore.description: How long the step waits after the previous step, in seconds, from '0' to '691200', which is 8 days. Defaults to '0'. Leave it out when the step waits until a time of day with `waitUntilTime`.

waitUntilDays.description: The days on which `waitUntilTime` applies, out of 'mon', 'tue', 'wed', 'thu', 'fri', 'sat' and 'sun'. Defaults to every day.

waitUntilTime.description: The time of day the step runs, in `HH:MM` format, instead of waiting `waitBefore`. Requires `waitUntilTimezone`. Responses show it in place of `waitBefore` on such steps.

waitUntilTimezone.description: The time zone of `waitUntilTime`, as a Rails time zone name such as `London` or `Eastern Time (US & Canada)`.

email.description: A User item's e-mail, returned for a User. A user can also be found by e-mail.

itemId.description: The catalog item's ID. For a user it's 'u123' or their e-mail. For a team it's 't123', and for any other item it's the item's own ID. Responses return users and teams in this form. Get a user's ID via [List team members](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/team-members/list/), and a team's ID via [List teams](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/teams/list/).

name.description: The catalog item's name. An item can also be found by its name instead of `itemId`.

type.description: `String`, 'no_value', or a catalog item's type, which is one of `User`, `Team`, `EscalationPolicy`, `OnCallSchedule`, `Monitor`, `SlackIntegration`, `LinearIntegration`, `JiraIntegration`, `MicrosoftTeamsIntegration`, `ZapierZap`, `OutgoingWebhook`, `PagerDutyIntegration` or `Source`. 'no_value' matches when the incident's metadata doesn't have the key or the key is empty.

value.description: The text of a `String` value.

email.description: The e-mail of a 'user' member, instead of its id.

id.description: The ID of the member's target. Required for 'user' unless `email` is set, and for 'policy', 'ai_sre' and every type that notifies one integration. A 'user' member is 'u123' or their e-mail, and responses return 'u123'. A 'current_on_call' member accepts an on-call calendar to notify instead of the team's default. An 'entire_team' member accepts another team in the organization, as its ID such as 't123'. Responses return it the same way. Both come back without an ID when they use the policy's own team. Get a user's ID via [List team members](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/team-members/list/), and a team's ID via [List teams](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/teams/list/).

metadataKey.description: The incident metadata key whose stored users, teams, on-call calendars, escalation policies and integrations an 'incident_metadata' member notifies.

type.description: The member type. 'current_on_call' notifies whoever is on call, and 'entire_team' everyone in the team. 'user' notifies one person, 'policy' runs another escalation policy, 'incident_metadata' notifies what the incident's metadata stores under `metadataKey`, and 'ai_sre' starts an AI SRE investigation. A member can also be one integration, with type 'webhook', 'email_integration', 'slack_integration', 'linear_integration', 'jira_integration', 'halo_psa_integration', 'microsoft_teams_integration', 'pagerduty_integration', 'zapier_webhook', 'zoom_integration' or 'google_meet_integration'. Or it can be every integration of one kind, with type 'all_slack_integrations', 'all_linear_integrations', 'all_jira_integrations', 'all_microsoft_teams_integrations', 'all_zapier_integrations', 'all_pagerduty_integrations', 'all_webhook_integrations', 'all_email_integrations', 'all_splunk_on_call_integrations', 'all_incident_io_integrations', 'all_zoom_integrations' or 'all_google_meet_integrations'.

chartType.description: Chart type. A funnel chart can switch only to the funnel trend chart, its trend over time, and back. 'line_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' and 'tail_query' queries. 'table_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' queries. 'bar_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' and 'tail_query' queries. 'number_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' and 'tail_query' queries. 'heatmap_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' queries. 'anomalies_chart': Accepts 'tail_query' queries. 'pie_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' queries. 'scatter_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' queries. 'gauge_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' and 'tail_query' queries. 'tail_chart': Accepts 'tail_query' queries. 'static_text_chart': Accepts a `staticText` query. 'map_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' queries. 'text_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' and 'tail_query' queries. 'funnel_chart': Accepts a `funnelQuery` query. 'funnel_trend_chart': Accepts a `funnelQuery` query. 'hierarchy_chart': Accepts 'sql_expression' queries.

treatMissingValues.description: How gaps in the data are drawn. Usually 'connected', 'disconnected', 'zero' or 'previous'.

treatZeroValues.description: How zero values are drawn, 'keep' or 'drop_disconnected'. Defaults to 'keep'.

unit.description: Unit the values are shown in, such as 'percent', 'bytes' or 'ms'. Table charts use `columnUnits` instead.

valueCategories.description: Label and color of each cell value of a categorized heatmap.

valueColumns.description: Result columns that hold the values to chart.

xAxisAnnotations.description: Vertical lines drawn at values on the X axis, each with a label and color. A value is a time or a number, as the X axis reads it.

xAxisType.description: How the X axis is read. Usually 'time', `value` or 'category'.

yAxisAnnotations.description: Horizontal lines drawn at values on the Y axis, each with a label and color.

yAxisAutoRange.description: How a line chart fits its Y axis when no bounds are set. Usually 'include_zero' or 'fit_data'.

yAxisMax.description: Highest value on the Y axis.

yAxisMin.description: Lowest value on the Y axis.

yAxisScale.description: Scale of the Y axis. Usually 'linear' or 'log'.

yAxisType.description: How the Y axis of a scatter chart is read. Usually `value` or 'category'.

customUnit.description: Whether `unit` is your own suffix, shown after the value as written and never scaled.

unit.description: Unit the column's values are shown in, such as 'auto', 'percent' or 'bytes'.

color.description: Color of the cells with the value, as a hex color such as `#22c55e`.

label.description: Text shown for the value.

color.description: The line's color, as a hex color such as `#22c55e`. Left out, the line is gray.

label.description: Text shown next to the line.

value.description: The X axis value the line is drawn at, a time or a number.

color.description: The line's color, as a hex color such as `#22c55e`. Left out, the line is gray.

label.description: Text shown next to the line.

value.description: The Y axis value the line is drawn at.

coordinates.description: Coordinate blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Read-only.

filters.description: Filter blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Read-only.

funnelQuery.description: A funnel's steps, session field and breakdown. Present only for `funnelQuery` queries. An update keeps the steps and fields it leaves out as they are.

groupBy.description: Grouping blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Read-only.

having.description: Having blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Read-only.

id.description: The query's ID.

name.description: The query's name.

orderBy.description: Ordering blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Read-only.

pointSize.description: Point size blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Read-only.

pqlQuery.description: The PQL the query is written in. Present only for 'pql_expression' queries.

queryType.description: Query type. You can replace a read-only query with a writable one, never edit it. Reads can also return 'promql_query', 'promql_v2_query' and 'promql_via_llm' for queries made in the app. 'sql_expression': A query written in SQL. You can write it through the API. 'tail_query': The filter of a tail chart. You can write it through the API. `staticText`: The text of a 'static_text_chart'. You can write it through the API. 'pql_expression': A query written in PQL. It's read-only. 'tail_query_builder': A tail chart's query made in the query builder. It's read-only. 'query_builder': A query made in the query builder. It's read-only. `funnelQuery`: A funnel's one query. You can write it through the API.

sourceVariable.description: The sources the query reads, either the name of a 'source' variable, such as 'source', or `source:` followed by specific sources. Defaults to 'source' on create. Omitted when not set.

sqlQuery.description: The SQL the query runs. Present for 'sql_expression', 'pql_expression', 'query_builder', 'tail_query_builder' and `funnelQuery` queries, and omitted when not set. Read-only except for 'sql_expression'.

staticText.description: The query's Markdown content. Present only for `staticText` queries, and omitted when not set.

where.description: Where blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Read-only.

whereCondition.description: The query's filter. Present only for 'tail_query' and 'tail_query_builder' queries, and omitted when not set.

xAxes.description: X-axis blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Read-only.

yAxes.description: Y-axis blocks of a 'query_builder' or 'tail_query_builder' query. Read-only.

allowMultipleValues.description: Whether a 'select_value' or 'select_with_sql' variable accepts more than one value at a time.

defaultValues.description: The variable's default values as strings, or an empty array when it has none.

filters.description: The saved filters of a 'select_predefined_sql' variable. Each has a `label` and an `sql` query, a complete query that returns one column with the filter's options.

name.description: The variable's name, used as `{{name}}` in queries.

selectedLabel.description: The label of the selected filter of a 'select_predefined_sql' variable. When not sent, the first filter is selected. A label that matches none of `filters` is refused.

sourceIds.description: The IDs of the sources a 'source' variable selects. They set the selection. Each must be a source the team can access.

sqlDefinition.description: The SQL expression whose distinct values are the options of a 'select_with_sql' variable, such as `JSONExtractString(raw, 'service')`. It runs against the variable's source over the selected range.

structuredValue.description: The variable's other settings, such as the selected sources of a 'source' variable in `canonicalSourceIds` and its services in `serviceIds`, or the saved filters of a 'select_predefined_sql' variable. Left out when not set.

values.description: The variable's current values as strings, or an empty array when it has none. For a 'source' variable, these are the IDs of the selected sources.

label.description: The filter's label, shown in the variable's menu.

sql.description: A complete query that returns one column with the filter's options.

canonicalSourceIds.description: Selected sources of a 'source' variable. Source IDs in `values` set them.

filters.description: Saved filters, each a label and the SQL that lists its values.

label.description: The filter's label, shown in the variable's menu.

sql.description: A complete query that returns one column with the filter's options.

email.description: Referenced user's e-mail, returned for a User. A user can also be found by e-mail.

itemId.description: ID of the referenced item. For a user it's 'u123' or their e-mail. For a team it's 't123', and for any other item it's the item's own ID. Responses return users and teams in this form. Get a user's ID via [List team members](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/team-members/list/), and a team's ID via [List teams](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/teams/list/).

name.description: Referenced item's name, or null when the item has no name or no longer exists. An item can also be found by its name instead of `itemId`.

type.description: `String`, or the type of the referenced item, which is one of `User`, `Team`, `EscalationPolicy`, `OnCallSchedule`, `Monitor`, `SlackIntegration`, `LinearIntegration`, `JiraIntegration`, `MicrosoftTeamsIntegration`, `ZapierZap`, `OutgoingWebhook`, `PagerDutyIntegration` or `Source`.

value.description: The text of a `String` value.

content.description: The text to extract around for 'match_before' and 'match_after', or the regular expression for 'match_regex'. Required for those three.

contentAfter.description: Where extraction stops for 'match_between'. Leave it empty to extract to the end.

fieldTarget.description: Which part of the notification to read. 'query_string': The query string of AWS's own HTTPS request, which never contains your message. 'header': A header of AWS's own HTTPS request, which never contains your message. 'body': The message your publisher sent, as plain text. 'json': A value in the message your publisher sent, read as JSON. 'xml': An element in the message your publisher sent, read as XML. 'sns_envelope': A value of the SNS envelope, such as its `Subject`.

matchType.description: What to extract. 'match_before': Extracts the text before `content`. 'match_after': Extracts the text after `content`. 'match_between': Extracts the text between `contentBefore` and `contentAfter`. 'match_regex': Extracts the match of the regular expression in `content`, or its capture group. 'match_everything': Extracts the whole value.

name.description: The metadata key a custom field's value is saved under. Custom fields require it, and it must be unique within its list. Not used by the cause, title and alert ID fields.

specialType.description: The built-in role of this field. null for a custom field. 'alert_id': Extracts the alert ID that ties later notifications to the same incident. 'cause': Extracts the incident cause. 'title': Extracts the incident title.

targetField.description: Which value to read. It's a dot-separated path such as `alert.id` for 'json' and 'query_string', a header name for 'header', a CSS selector for 'xml', or `TopicArn`, `MessageId` or `Subject` for 'sns_envelope'. Not used with 'body'.

content.description: The value to compare with. Must be a valid regular expression for 'matches_regex' and 'matches_regex_not'.

matchType.description: How to compare the value with `content`. 'contains': Matches when the value contains `content`. 'contains_not': Matches when the value doesn't contain `content`. 'matches_regex': Matches when the value matches the regular expression in `content`. 'matches_regex_not': Matches when the value doesn't match the regular expression in `content`. 'equals': Matches when the value equals `content`. 'equals_not': Matches when the value doesn't equal `content`.

ruleTarget.description: Which part of the notification the rule checks. 'query_string': The query string of AWS's own HTTPS request, which never contains your message. 'header': A header of AWS's own HTTPS request, which never contains your message. 'body': The message your publisher sent, as plain text. 'json': A value in the message your publisher sent, read as JSON. 'xml': An element in the message your publisher sent, read as XML. 'sns_envelope': A value of the SNS envelope, such as its `Subject`.

codeMappingSourceRoot.description: The path from your repository's root to the deployed source code, such as `apps/backend/`. A stack frame's path under `codeMappingStackRoot` is looked up under this path in the linked repository.

codeMappingStackRoot.description: The absolute path to the root of the stack trace on your server, such as `/usr/src/app/`. Stack frames under it are mapped to files in the linked repository.

correlateWithSourceId.description: The telemetry source, from [List sources](https://betterstack.com/docs/logs/api/list-all-existing-sources/), whose logs and traces are correlated with these errors.

customBucket.description: Your own S3-compatible bucket to archive data in, or null when the application uses Better Stack storage. Changing only `accessKeyId` and `secretAccessKey` rotates the bucket's key pair. Changing `name`, `endpoint` or `keepDataAfterRetention`, or adding or removing it, replaces the resource.

dataRegion.description: The data region. It's 'europe', 'us', 'singapore' or a dedicated cluster's name from [List data regions](https://betterstack.com/docs/errors/api/data-regions/). An application created with `correlateWithSourceId` uses that source's region, and a different region here is refused. Omit it to use the organization's default.

deletionProtection.description: Whether destroying or replacing this application is refused. Defaults to true. Set it to false and apply before you delete or replace it on purpose. It's kept in state and never sent to Better Stack.

errorsRetention.description: Days to keep errors. Accepts one of the retention periods your plan offers, or the value already set. Defaults to your plan's default retention, or to a longer one the team's other applications already use.

githubRepositoryName.description: The linked GitHub repository for source-code mapping, as `owner/name`, such as `acme/web`. Connect it to your team with the [GitHub integration](https://betterstack.com/docs/errors/integrations/github/) first. Set it to an empty string to disconnect it. Can't be set together with `gitlabRepositoryName`.

gitlabRepositoryName.description: The linked GitLab repository for source-code mapping, as `group/name`, such as `acme/web`, from the team's connected repositories. Set it to an empty string to disconnect it. Can't be set together with `githubRepositoryName`.

ingestingPaused.description: Whether ingestion is paused for this application. Defaults to false.

jsTagConfiguration.description: Settings of the JavaScript tag, as on the application's **Frontend** page. It's null for an application without a JavaScript tag.

jsTagOwnDomainStatus.description: Whether the CNAME record of your own subdomain points to `proxy.betterstack.net`. It's null when `jsTagConfiguration` has no `ownDomain`. 'checking': Better Stack hasn't checked the CNAME record since the subdomain last changed. 'missing': The subdomain has no CNAME record. 'invalid': The CNAME record doesn't point to `proxy.betterstack.net`. 'valid': The CNAME record points to `proxy.betterstack.net`, so the tag is served from the subdomain.

jsTagToken.description: Token of the browser tag, separate from `token`. It's the `?t=` value the `/b.js` browser tag is loaded with. null for a platform without a browser tag. To print it, export it as a stack output and run pulumi stack output with its name and --show-secrets.

replaysRetention.description: Days to keep session replays. Accepts one of the retention periods your plan offers, or the value already set. A change applies to every application connected to the same source. Only an application that records session replays accepts it.

sourceTypes.description: Row types the application holds, such as 'exceptions', 'logs', 'metrics', `replays`, 'spans' or `webEvents`, sorted by name.

token.description: Ingestion token. It's the DSN to configure your SDK with. To print it, export it as a stack output and run pulumi stack output with its name and --show-secrets.

attributes.description: The relation's attributes, in the order the web app shows them as columns. List primary attributes first, since primary attributes always come before the others. Required on create, and at least one must be primary. An update replaces all attributes with the list, and attributes it leaves out are removed with their values from every record. An update without the list keeps the attributes as they are. In Pulumi, an item without an id keeps the id of the existing item with the same `name`, so a reorder or a move updates it in place. An item that matches none keeps the id of the existing item at its position when no other item took that one, so a rename updates it in place too.

matchMode.description: How primary attributes combine when matching records. Defaults to 'any'. 'any': Matches a record when any primary attribute matches. 'all': Matches a record when every primary attribute matches.

blockedMetrics.description: Metric names marked as spam, which are dropped when they're ingested. Read more about [marking metrics as spam](https://betterstack.com/docs/logs/using-logtail/transforming-ingested-data/mark-metrics-as-spam/).

collectorLogsTransformation.description: VRL program the collector runs on each log line on your hardware, before sending it to Better Stack. Remove the argument to clear it.

collectorMetricsTransformation.description: VRL program the collector runs on each metric on your hardware, before sending it to Better Stack. Remove the argument to clear it.

collectorTracesTransformation.description: VRL program the collector runs on each span on your hardware, before sending it to Better Stack. Remove the argument to clear it.

configuration.description: Collector configuration. It says which components are on, plus sampling rates, batching and buffering. An update merges the components it includes into the stored ones.

connectedSourceIds.description: IDs of the sources connected to this collector's source to correlate their logs and traces. A connection goes both ways. The collector's source joins the listed sources and the sources they're already connected to. No existing connection is removed, and `[]` disconnects the collector's source.

customBucket.description: Your own S3-compatible bucket to archive data in, or null when the collector uses Better Stack storage. Read more about [hosting data in your own bucket](https://betterstack.com/docs/logs/host-data-in-your-own-bucket/). Set it on create. An update that sets only `accessKeyId` and `secretAccessKey` rotates its key pair. Changing `name`, `endpoint` or `keepDataAfterRetention`, or adding or removing it, replaces the resource.

dataRegion.description: The data region, 'europe', 'us', 'singapore' or a dedicated cluster's name from [List data regions](https://betterstack.com/docs/logs/api/data-regions/). It reads back as that name. It can't be changed after the collector is created. Defaults to the organization's default data region.

deletionProtection.description: Whether destroying or replacing this collector is refused. Defaults to true. Set it to false and apply before you delete or replace it on purpose. It's kept in state and never sent to Better Stack.

ingestingPaused.description: Whether ingestion is paused for this collector. Defaults to false.

ingestionLogsTransformation.description: VRL program Better Stack runs on each log line from the collector as it's ingested. Remove the argument to clear it.

ingestionTracesTransformation.description: VRL program Better Stack runs on each span from the collector as it's ingested. Remove the argument to clear it.

installationGuideUrl.description: Link to the installation guide for the collector's platform, with the install command that uses its `secret`.

liveTailPattern.description: The pattern Live tail shows each log line with. Columns are wrapped in braces, such as `PID: {message_json.pid} {level} {message}`. It's null when the collector's source doesn't receive logs. See [Formatting logs](https://betterstack.com/docs/logs/using-logtail/formatting-logs/). A collector whose source doesn't receive logs refuses it.

liveTailPatternSpans.description: The pattern Live tail shows each span with. Columns are wrapped in braces, such as `{span.name} {duration}`. It's null when the collector's source doesn't receive spans. See [Formatting logs](https://betterstack.com/docs/logs/using-logtail/formatting-logs/). A collector whose source doesn't receive spans refuses it.

logsRetention.description: Days logs are kept, one of the retention periods your plan offers.

metricsRetention.description: Days metrics are kept, one of the retention periods your plan offers.

name.description: Collector name.

note.description: A note about the collector. Remove the argument to clear it.

pingedAt.description: When a host of the collector last checked in, or null when no host has checked in yet.

platform.description: Where the collector runs. Can't be changed after the collector is created. Valid values: 'docker', 'swarm', 'kubernetes'.

secret.description: Secret the deployed collector authenticates with. Returned on every read. To print it, export it as a stack output and run pulumi stack output with its name and --show-secrets.

serviceFields.description: Log fields that break data down by service. Each entry needs a `nameKey`, and `typeKey` can be null to skip it. The list replaces the existing one, and `[]` removes them all.

sourceGroupId.description: Source group the collector's source belongs to, or null when it's in no group. Get the IDs via [List source groups](https://betterstack.com/docs/logs/api/list-all-existing-source-groups/).

sourceId.description: ID of the source the collector sends data to.

status.description: The collector's status, worked out from its hosts, one of 'pending', 'up', 'degraded', 'unknown', 'partially_up', 'unsupported_version' or 'down'.

teamId.description: Team that owns the collector, such as 't123'. Defaults to the provider's `teamId`. Set it to create this object in another team. Changing it replaces the resource, because an object can't move to another team.

teamName.description: Name of the team that owns the collector.

updatedAt.description: When the collector was last updated.

userVectorConfig.description: Your own Vector configuration in YAML, merged into the configuration the collector runs with.

status.description: The connection status. An update that includes `host`, `port`, `service`, `listenIp`, `endpoint`, `scheme`, `username`, `password`, `apiKey`, `sslMode` or `tls` sets it back to 'pending'. 'down': The collector reaches the target, but its check fails. 'invalid_credentials': The target rejects the credentials. 'configuration_required': Metrics are collected, but the database needs more setup, such as the 'pg_stat_statements' extension. 'disabled': The target is paused and the collector doesn't check it. 'removed': The collector no longer finds the target.

With it, creating a dashboard accepts `name`, `product`, `sourceId`, either `dashboardGroupId` or `resourceGroupName`, and `refreshInterval`, `dateRangeFrom`, `dateRangeTo` and `sourceEligibilitySql`, which replace the template's. It doesn't accept `variables`. Better Stack never returns it, so Pulumi keeps the value you set.

variables.description: The dashboard's variables, which chart queries use by name, such as `{{source}}`. Returned when you get one dashboard. Creating a dashboard adds any of the built-in 'time', 'start_time', 'end_time' and 'source' variables the list leaves out. An update replaces all variables. Any the list leaves out is removed, except the built-in 'time', 'start_time', 'end_time' and 'source' variables, which always exist. The built-in variables keep their own type. A listed variable that already exists keeps the `variableType`, `defaultValues`, `sqlDefinition`, `structuredValue` and `allowMultipleValues` it leaves out, and null clears any of them except `variableType`. Its `values` aren't kept, so list them again, except on a 'source' variable, which keeps its sources while it leaves out both `values` and `structuredValue`. Changing `variableType` clears the old `defaultValues`, `sqlDefinition` and `structuredValue`. See [Query variables](https://betterstack.com/docs/logs/dashboards/variables/). `sqlDefinition` is accepted only on 'select_with_sql' and 'multi_select_with_sql' variables. When a variable is saved with empty `values`, a 'select_value' gets the first of its `defaultValues`, a 'string', 'number', 'boolean' or 'sql_expression' gets all of them, and a 'select_with_sql' whose `sqlDefinition` is new or changed gets the first option it returns. An ISO 8601 date in a 'date' or 'datetime' variable is saved in `values` as a Unix timestamp in microseconds. A new or changed `sqlDefinition` or filter `sql` runs against the selected source, and the change is refused when the query fails.

templateId.description: ID of the dashboard template to create the dashboard from, as [List dashboard templates](https://betterstack.com/docs/logs/api/dashboards/templates/) lists it. The dashboard starts with the template's charts, sections, alerts, variables and settings. With it, creating a dashboard accepts `name`, `product`, `sourceId`, either `dashboardGroupId` or `resourceGroupName`, and `refreshInterval`, `dateRangeFrom`, `dateRangeTo` and `sourceEligibilitySql`, which replace the template's. It doesn't accept `variables`. Better Stack never returns it, so Pulumi keeps the value you set.

variables.description: The dashboard's variables, which chart queries use by name, such as `{{source}}`. Returned when you get one dashboard. Creating a dashboard adds any of the built-in 'time', 'start_time', 'end_time' and 'source' variables the list leaves out. An update replaces all variables. Any the list leaves out is removed, except the built-in 'time', 'start_time', 'end_time' and 'source' variables, which always exist. The built-in variables keep their own type. A listed variable that already exists keeps the `variableType`, `defaultValues`, `sqlDefinition`, `structuredValue` and `allowMultipleValues` it leaves out, and null clears any of them except `variableType`. Its `values` aren't kept, so list them again, except on a 'source' variable, which keeps its sources while it leaves out both `values` and `structuredValue`. Changing `variableType` clears the old `defaultValues`, `sqlDefinition` and `structuredValue`. See [Query variables](https://betterstack.com/docs/logs/dashboards/variables/). `sqlDefinition` is accepted only on 'select_with_sql' and 'multi_select_with_sql' variables. When a variable is saved with empty `values`, a 'select_value' gets the first of its `defaultValues`, a 'string', 'number', 'boolean' or 'sql_expression' gets all of them, and a 'select_with_sql' whose `sqlDefinition` is new or changed gets the first option it returns. An ISO 8601 date in a 'date' or 'datetime' variable is saved in `values` as a Unix timestamp in microseconds. A new or changed `sqlDefinition` or filter `sql` runs against the selected source, and the change is refused when the query fails.

dateRangeFrom.description: Start of the default date range, such as `now-3h`. A funnel's defaults to `now-7d`. It's applied only when sent, so it can't be cleared. Defaults to `now-3h`.

dateRangeTo.description: Default range end, for example now. Applied only when sent, so it can't be cleared. Defaults to 'now'.

explorationGroupId.description: Group this exploration belongs to. Remove the argument or set it to `"0"` to clear it from its group.

name.description: Exploration name. While it's still the default, a name generated from the query is returned. The chart is named after it, so the chart's name is never sent.

product.description: The Explore the exploration lives in. Leave it out on create to put the exploration in Telemetry's Explore. A funnel over web events goes in RUM's Explore instead. Changing it moves the exploration to the other Explore. 'telemetry': Telemetry's Explore. 'rum': RUM's Explore, which reads an application's web events only.

queries.description: The chart's queries, in ID order. Updating an exploration replaces all of its queries. Each query accepts only the keys its `queryType` uses. A 'sql_expression' query uses `sqlQuery` and `sourceVariable`. A 'tail_query' uses `whereCondition` and `sourceVariable`. A `staticText` query uses `staticText`, and a `funnelQuery` uses `funnelQuery`. A key another type uses, or more than one query on a chart other than 'line_chart', is refused.

sourceId.description: ID of the source a funnel reads. Required when creating a funnel, and accepted only then. Other explorations pick their sources in the 'source' variable. Better Stack never returns it, so Pulumi keeps the value you set.

sourceType.description: The events a funnel reads from its source. When it's left out or the source doesn't have them, the funnel reads web events, logs or spans, the first of them the source has. Valid values: 'web_events', 'logs', 'spans'. Better Stack never returns it, so Pulumi keeps the value you set.

teamName.description: Name of the team that owns the exploration.

updatedAt.description: When the exploration was last updated.

variables.description: Template variables. An update replaces all variables. Any the list leaves out is removed, except the built-in 'time', 'start_time', 'end_time' and 'source' variables, which always exist. A listed variable without `defaultValues`, `sqlDefinition` or `structuredValue` keeps the stored ones while its `variableType` stays the same, and a new `variableType` clears them. One sent without `values` gets empty `values`, except a 'source' variable, which keeps its sources while it leaves out both `values` and `structuredValue`. One sent without `allowMultipleValues` keeps the stored flag. `sqlDefinition` applies only to 'select_with_sql' and 'multi_select_with_sql' variables. `allowMultipleValues` is saved only for 'select_value' and 'select_with_sql' variables. When a variable is saved with empty `values`, a 'select_value' gets the first of its `defaultValues`, a 'string', 'number', 'boolean' or 'sql_expression' gets all of them, and a 'select_with_sql' whose `sqlDefinition` is new or changed gets the first option it returns. An ISO 8601 date in a 'date' or 'datetime' variable is saved in `values` as a Unix timestamp in microseconds. A new or changed `sqlDefinition` or filter `sql` runs against the selected source, and the change is refused when the query fails. A 'source' variable's values are IDs of sources the team can access. In a 'rum' exploration, pick each source as its web events, `:web_events`. A funnel can't have variables. Its source is set in `sourceId`. See [Query variables](https://betterstack.com/docs/logs/dashboards/variables/).

queries.description: The chart's queries, in ID order. Updating an exploration replaces all of its queries. Each query accepts only the keys its `queryType` uses. A 'sql_expression' query uses `sqlQuery` and `sourceVariable`. A 'tail_query' uses `whereCondition` and `sourceVariable`. A `staticText` query uses `staticText`, and a `funnelQuery` uses `funnelQuery`. A key another type uses, or more than one query on a chart other than 'line_chart', is refused.

sourceId.description: ID of the source a funnel reads. Required when creating a funnel, and accepted only then. Other explorations pick their sources in the 'source' variable. Better Stack never returns it, so Pulumi keeps the value you set.

sourceType.description: The events a funnel reads from its source. When it's left out or the source doesn't have them, the funnel reads web events, logs or spans, the first of them the source has. Valid values: 'web_events', 'logs', 'spans'. Better Stack never returns it, so Pulumi keeps the value you set.

teamId.description: Team that owns the exploration, such as 't123'. Defaults to the provider's `teamId`. Set it to create this object in another team. Changing it replaces the resource, because an object can't move to another team.

teamName.description: Name of the team that owns the exploration.

updatedAt.description: When the exploration was last updated.

variables.description: Template variables. An update replaces all variables. Any the list leaves out is removed, except the built-in 'time', 'start_time', 'end_time' and 'source' variables, which always exist. A listed variable without `defaultValues`, `sqlDefinition` or `structuredValue` keeps the stored ones while its `variableType` stays the same, and a new `variableType` clears them. One sent without `values` gets empty `values`, except a 'source' variable, which keeps its sources while it leaves out both `values` and `structuredValue`. One sent without `allowMultipleValues` keeps the stored flag. `sqlDefinition` applies only to 'select_with_sql' and 'multi_select_with_sql' variables. `allowMultipleValues` is saved only for 'select_value' and 'select_with_sql' variables. When a variable is saved with empty `values`, a 'select_value' gets the first of its `defaultValues`, a 'string', 'number', 'boolean' or 'sql_expression' gets all of them, and a 'select_with_sql' whose `sqlDefinition` is new or changed gets the first option it returns. An ISO 8601 date in a 'date' or 'datetime' variable is saved in `values` as a Unix timestamp in microseconds. A new or changed `sqlDefinition` or filter `sql` runs against the selected source, and the change is refused when the query fails. A 'source' variable's values are IDs of sources the team can access. In a 'rum' exploration, pick each source as its web events, `:web_events`. A funnel can't have variables. Its source is set in `sourceId`. See [Query variables](https://betterstack.com/docs/logs/dashboards/variables/).

name.description: The name of the Amazon SNS integration shown in the dashboard.

otherAcknowledgedFields.description: Custom fields extracted from an acknowledging payload.

otherResolvedFields.description: Custom fields extracted from a resolving payload.

otherStartedFields.description: Custom fields extracted from a started payload, stored as incident metadata.

paused.description: Whether the integration is paused. A paused integration opens no incidents. Defaults to false.

push.description: Whether to send a push notification to the on-call person. Ignored while an escalation policy is set. Defaults to false.

recoveryPeriod.description: Seconds a matching resolved payload must hold before the incident resolves. It applies only while `resolvedRuleType` isn't 'unused'. Valid values: '0', '60', '180', '300', '900', '1800', '3600', '7200'. Defaults to '0'.

resolvedAlertIdField.description: How to extract the alert ID from a notification that resolves an incident, with the same keys as `causeField`. Required when `resolvedRuleType` isn't 'unused'.

resolvedRuleType.description: When notifications resolve an incident. Any value other than 'unused' needs `startedAlertIdField`, `resolvedAlertIdField` and at least one rule. Resolving is checked first, then acknowledging, then opening, and a notification that matches no open incident can still open one. Defaults to 'unused'. 'unused': Notifications never resolve an incident. 'any': A notification resolves an incident when at least one of `resolvedRules` matches. 'all': A notification resolves an incident when all of `resolvedRules` match.

resolvedRules.description: The conditions `resolvedRuleType` checks, with the same keys as `startedRules`. At least one is required when the type is 'any' or 'all'.

sms.description: Whether to send an SMS to the on-call person. Ignored while an escalation policy is set. Defaults to false.

startedAlertIdField.description: How to extract the alert ID from the notification that starts an incident, with the same keys as `causeField`. Later notifications acknowledge or resolve the open incident with the same alert ID. Required when `acknowledgedRuleType` or `resolvedRuleType` isn't 'unused'.

startedRuleType.description: When notifications open an incident. Every value other than 'unused' needs at least one rule. When `startedAlertIdField` finds an alert ID that matches an open incident, the notification goes to that incident instead of opening a new one. Defaults to 'unused'. 'unused': Every notification that doesn't acknowledge or resolve an incident opens one. 'any': A notification opens an incident when at least one of `startedRules` matches. 'all': A notification opens an incident when all of `startedRules` match.

startedRules.description: The conditions `startedRuleType` checks. At least one rule is required when the type is 'any' or 'all'.

subscriptionState.description: Whether AWS has confirmed the SNS subscription. 'awaiting': AWS hasn't confirmed the subscription yet. 'active': AWS has confirmed the subscription.

teamWait.description: Seconds to wait before escalating to the whole team. '0' alerts the whole team right away, and null never escalates to the team. Ignored while an escalation policy is set.

titleField.description: How to extract a custom incident title from the notification that starts an incident, with the same keys as `causeField`.
