metadata.description: Custom metadata. Each key holds a list of values. A value is a string, written as `{type: "String", value}`, or a catalog reference, written as `{type, item_id, name, email}`. User references are returned as 'u123' and team references as 't123'. Get a user's ID via [List team members](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/team-members/list/), and a team's ID via [List teams](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/teams/list/). A key accepts a single value or a list. Values under one key must all be the same type and can't repeat. An update replaces all of the integration's metadata with the object, `{}` removes it all, and leaving `metadata` out keeps it. Each key holds its list under `values`.

name.description: The name of the Amazon SNS integration shown in the dashboard.

otherAcknowledgedFields.description: Custom fields extracted from an acknowledging payload.

otherResolvedFields.description: Custom fields extracted from a resolving payload.

otherStartedFields.description: Custom fields extracted from a started payload, stored as incident metadata.

paused.description: Whether the integration is paused. A paused integration opens no incidents. Defaults to false.

push.description: Whether to send a push notification to the on-call person. Ignored while an escalation policy is set. Defaults to false.

recoveryPeriod.description: Seconds a matching resolved payload must hold before the incident resolves. It applies only while `resolvedRuleType` isn't 'unused'. Valid values: '0', '60', '180', '300', '900', '1800', '3600', '7200'. Defaults to '0'.

resolvedAlertIdField.description: How to extract the alert ID from a notification that resolves an incident, with the same keys as `causeField`. Required when `resolvedRuleType` isn't 'unused'.

resolvedRuleType.description: When notifications resolve an incident. Any value other than 'unused' needs `startedAlertIdField`, `resolvedAlertIdField` and at least one rule. Resolving is checked first, then acknowledging, then opening, and a notification that matches no open incident can still open one. Defaults to 'unused'. 'unused': Notifications never resolve an incident. 'any': A notification resolves an incident when at least one of `resolvedRules` matches. 'all': A notification resolves an incident when all of `resolvedRules` match.

resolvedRules.description: The conditions `resolvedRuleType` checks, with the same keys as `startedRules`. At least one is required when the type is 'any' or 'all'.

sms.description: Whether to send an SMS to the on-call person. Ignored while an escalation policy is set. Defaults to false.

startedAlertIdField.description: How to extract the alert ID from the notification that starts an incident, with the same keys as `causeField`. Later notifications acknowledge or resolve the open incident with the same alert ID. Required when `acknowledgedRuleType` or `resolvedRuleType` isn't 'unused'.

startedRuleType.description: When notifications open an incident. Every value other than 'unused' needs at least one rule. When `startedAlertIdField` finds an alert ID that matches an open incident, the notification goes to that incident instead of opening a new one. Defaults to 'unused'. 'unused': Every notification that doesn't acknowledge or resolve an incident opens one. 'any': A notification opens an incident when at least one of `startedRules` matches. 'all': A notification opens an incident when all of `startedRules` match.

startedRules.description: The conditions `startedRuleType` checks. At least one rule is required when the type is 'any' or 'all'.

teamId.description: Team that owns this integration, such as 't123'. Defaults to the provider's `teamId`. Set it to create this object in another team. Changing it replaces the resource, because an object can't move to another team.

teamWait.description: Seconds to wait before escalating to the whole team. '0' alerts the whole team right away, and null never escalates to the team. Ignored while an escalation policy is set.

titleField.description: How to extract a custom incident title from the notification that starts an incident, with the same keys as `causeField`. The dashboard's default extracts the whole SNS `Subject`, with `fieldTarget` set to 'sns_envelope', `targetField` to `Subject` and `matchType` to 'match_everything'. null extracts no title. Leaving it out clears it, on create too.

Without it, an 'incident_change' or 'monitor_change' webhook sends the incident or monitor under 'data', with what happened in 'event', such as 'started' or 'created'. 'plan_minimum': Your plan's shortest interval between checks is longer than `checkFrequency`, which was saved before the plan changed. `requestTimeout`: The monitor's `requestTimeout` is longer than `checkFrequency`.

maintenanceFrom.description: Start of the daily maintenance window, when we don't check, as `HH:MM:SS`, like `01:00:00`. null when no window is set.

maintenanceTimezone.description: The time zone of the maintenance window, as a Rails time zone name like `Amsterdam` or its IANA ID like `Europe/Amsterdam`. null when it isn't set, which works as UTC. Defaults to `UTC`.

maintenanceTo.description: End of the daily maintenance window, as `HH:MM:SS`, like `03:00:00`. Required with `maintenanceFrom`. null when no window is set.

metadata.description: Custom metadata. Each key holds a list of values. A value is a string, written as `{type: "String", value}`, or a catalog reference, written as `{type, item_id, name, email}`. User references are returned as 'u123' and team references as 't123'. Get a user's ID via [List team members](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/team-members/list/), and a team's ID via [List teams](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/teams/list/). Values under one key must all be the same type and can't repeat. Each key holds its list under `values`.

monitorGroupId.description: ID of the monitor group this monitor belongs to.

monitorType.description: What the monitor checks. Defaults to 'status'. `status`: Checks that the URL returns a 2XX status code. 'expected_status_code': Checks that the URL returns one of `expectedStatusCodes`. 'keyword': Checks that the page contains `requiredKeyword`. 'keyword_absence': Checks that the page doesn't contain `requiredKeyword`. 'ping': Pings the host in `url`. 'tcp': Checks that a TCP `port` on the host accepts connections. 'udp': Sends `requestBody` to a UDP `port` on the host and checks that the answer contains `requiredKeyword`. 'smtp': Checks for an SMTP server on the host at `port`. 'pop': Checks for a POP3 server on the host at `port`. 'imap': Checks for an IMAP server on the host at `port`. 'dns': Checks that the DNS server on the host answers a query for the domain in `requestBody`. 'playwright': Runs the scenario in `playwrightScript`.

paused.description: Whether the monitor is paused. A paused monitor opens no incidents and sends no alerts. Set it to true to pause it or false to resume it. Defaults to false.

playwrightScript.description: The JavaScript source of the scenario, for 'playwright' monitors.

port.description: The port to check. 'tcp' and 'udp' accept one port. 'smtp' accepts '25', '465' or '587', 'pop' accepts '110' or '995', and 'imap' accepts '143' or '993', with several separated by commas like `25,465,587`. Required for 'tcp', 'udp', 'smtp', 'pop' and 'imap' monitors.

pronounceableName.description: The name of the monitor, which we use when we call you.

proxyHost.description: The host of the proxy server we send the check through, without a protocol. It can include credentials, like `user:pass@proxy.example.com`. Only for `status`, 'expected_status_code', 'keyword' and 'keyword_absence' monitors.

proxyPort.description: The port of the proxy server, from '1' to '65535'. Requires `proxyHost`.

push.description: Whether to send a push notification to the on-call person. Ignored while an escalation policy is set. Defaults to false.

recoveryPeriod.description: How long checks must keep passing before the incident resolves, in seconds. Valid values: '0', '60', '180', '300', '900', '1800', '3600', '7200'. Defaults to '180'.

regions.description: Regions to check from, as any combination of 'us', 'eu', 'as' and 'au'. When none are set, we check from all regions. Responses then list all of them.

rememberCookies.description: Whether we keep cookies when redirecting. Defaults to true.

requestBody.description: The body of the request. A 'dns' monitor requires it. Set it to the domain to query. A 'udp' monitor sends it as its content. Must be empty for 'get', 'head' and 'options' requests.

requestHeaders.description: Custom request headers, as a list of `{name, value}` objects. A list replaces all headers, and an empty list removes them all.

requestTimeout.description: How long a check waits before it times out. Its unit and accepted values depend on `monitorType`. `status`, 'expected_status_code', 'keyword' and 'keyword_absence': In seconds. It accepts '2', '3', '5', '10', '15', '30', '45', '60', '90', '120' or '180' and defaults to '30'. 'ping', 'tcp', 'udp', 'smtp', 'pop', 'imap' and 'dns': In milliseconds. It accepts '500', '1000', '2000', '3000' or '5000' and defaults to '5000'. 'playwright': In seconds. requiredKeyword.description: The keyword to look for. Required for 'keyword', 'keyword_absence' and 'udp' monitors.

scenarioName.description: The name of a 'playwright' monitor's scenario. Required for 'playwright' monitors, and returned only for them. At least one of `url` or `scenarioName` must be configured.

sms.description: Whether to send an SMS to the on-call person. Ignored while an escalation policy is set. Defaults to false.

sslExpiration.description: How many days before the SSL certificate expires we alert you. null turns the check off and is the default. collectorId.description: The ID of the parent this collector belongs to. Changing it replaces the resource.

enabled.description: Whether the collector scrapes this target. A new target is enabled unless it's set to false. Disabling it sets `status` to 'disabled', and enabling it again checks the target again.

endpoint.description: The full scrape URL, like `http://10.0.0.5:9090/metrics`. Required for 'prometheus' targets and returned only for them. Applies only when `kind` is 'prometheus'.

host.description: Target host. For the process kinds this is the host the collector runs on.

id.description: The ID of the collector target to look up.

kind.description: Target type. Reads can also return 'pgcat', 'node_exporter' and 'kube_state_metrics', which the collector finds by itself and the API doesn't accept on create. Valid values: 'postgres', 'pgbouncer', 'mysql', 'redis', 'mongodb', 'memcached', 'elasticsearch', 'nginx', 'apache', 'kafka', 'prometheus', 'traefik'.

listenIp.description: The IP address the process listens on. Accepted and returned only for 'nginx', 'apache', 'kafka' and 'traefik', and null when not set. Applies only when `kind` is 'nginx' or 'apache' or 'kafka' or 'traefik'.

port.description: The target's port. null when a target is found by its `listenIp` or `service` instead. Applies only when `kind` is 'postgres' or 'pgbouncer' or 'mysql' or 'redis' or 'mongodb' or 'memcached' or 'elasticsearch' or 'nginx' or 'apache' or 'kafka' or 'traefik'.

scheme.description: The connection scheme. Accepted and returned only for 'elasticsearch'. Valid values: 'http', 'https'. Applies only when `kind` is 'elasticsearch'.

service.description: The service name. Required for 'nginx', 'apache', 'kafka', 'prometheus' and 'traefik' targets, and accepted and returned only for those. Applies only when `kind` is 'nginx' or 'apache' or 'kafka' or 'prometheus' or 'traefik'.

sslMode.description: The SSL mode for the connection. Required for 'postgres' and 'pgbouncer', and accepted and returned only for those. Applies only when `kind` is 'postgres' or 'pgbouncer'. 'disable': Connects without SSL. 'require': Connects over SSL without verifying the server's certificate. `verify-ca`: Connects over SSL and checks that a trusted certificate authority signed the server's certificate.

status.description: The connection status. An update that includes `host`, `port`, `service`, `listenIp`, `endpoint`, `scheme`, `username`, `password`, `apiKey`, `sslMode` or `tls` sets it back to 'pending'. 'pending': The collector hasn't reported on the target yet. 'up': The collector collects metrics from the target. 'unreachable': The collector can't connect to the target or hasn't seen it lately. 'down': The collector reaches the target, but its check fails. 'invalid_credentials': The target rejects the credentials. 'configuration_required': Metrics are collected, but the database needs more setup, such as the 'pg_stat_statements' extension. 'disabled': The target is paused and the collector doesn't check it. 'removed': The collector no longer finds the target.

teamId.description: Team that owns the collector's source, such as 't123'. Defaults to the provider's `teamId`. Set it to look the object up in another team.

tls.description: The TLS mode for the connection. Required for 'mysql', and accepted and returned only for it. Applies only when `kind` is 'mysql'. false: Connects without TLS. true: Connects over TLS and verifies the server's certificate. `skip-verify`: Connects over TLS without verifying the server's certificate. 'preferred': Uses TLS when the server supports it, without verifying the server's certificate.

updatedAt.description: When the target was last updated.

username.description: The username used to connect, or null when not set. Accepted and returned only for 'postgres', 'pgbouncer', 'mysql', 'redis', 'mongodb', 'memcached' and 'elasticsearch'. Applies only when `kind` is 'postgres' or 'pgbouncer' or 'mysql' or 'redis' or 'mongodb' or 'memcached' or 'elasticsearch'.

acknowledgedAlertIdField.description: How to extract the alert ID from an e-mail that acknowledges an incident, with the same keys as `causeField`. Required when `acknowledgedRuleType` isn't 'unused'.

acknowledgedRuleType.description: When e-mails acknowledge an incident. Any value other than 'unused' needs `startedAlertIdField`, `acknowledgedAlertIdField` and at least one rule. 'unused': E-mails never acknowledge an incident. 'any': An e-mail acknowledges an incident when at least one of `acknowledgedRules` matches. 'all': An e-mail acknowledges an incident when all of `acknowledgedRules` match.

acknowledgedRules.description: The conditions `acknowledgedRuleType` checks, with the same keys as `startedRules`. At least one is required when the type is 'any' or 'all'.

call.description: Whether to call the on-call person. Ignored while an escalation policy is set.

causeField.description: How to extract the incident cause from the e-mail that starts an incident. Defaults to the whole subject.

criticalAlert.description: Whether to send a critical push notification that ignores the mute switch and Do Not Disturb mode. Ignored while an escalation policy is set.

email.description: Whether to send an e-mail to the on-call person. Ignored while an escalation policy is set.

emailAddress.description: The address to forward your e-mails to. E-mails sent to it open incidents.

escalationPolicyId.description: ID of the escalation policy for alerts, or null to alert the current on-call person directly. Returned as a string.

id.description: The ID of the incoming e-mail integration to look up.

metadata.description: Custom metadata. Each key holds a list of values. A value is a string, written as `{type: "String", value}`, or a catalog reference, written as `{type, item_id, name, email}`. User references are returned as 'u123' and team references as 't123'. Get a user's ID via [List team members](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/team-members/list/), and a team's ID via [List teams](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/teams/list/). A key accepts a single value or a list. Values under one key must all be the same type and can't repeat. Each key holds its list under `values`.

name.description: The name of the e-mail integration shown in the dashboard.

otherAcknowledgedFields.description: Custom fields extracted from an acknowledging e-mail.

otherResolvedFields.description: Custom fields extracted from a resolving e-mail.

otherStartedFields.description: Custom fields extracted from a started e-mail, stored as incident metadata.

paused.description: Whether the integration is paused. A paused integration opens no incidents.

push.description: Whether to send a push notification to the on-call person. Ignored while an escalation policy is set.

recoveryPeriod.description: Seconds a matching resolved e-mail must hold before the incident resolves. It applies only while `resolvedRuleType` isn't 'unused'. Valid values: '0', '60', '180', '300', '900', '1800', '3600', '7200'.

resolvedAlertIdField.description: How to extract the alert ID from an e-mail that resolves an incident, with the same keys as `causeField`. Required when `resolvedRuleType` isn't 'unused'.

resolvedRuleType.description: When e-mails resolve an incident. Any value other than 'unused' needs `startedAlertIdField`, `resolvedAlertIdField` and at least one rule. Resolving is checked first, then acknowledging, then opening, and an e-mail that matches no open incident can still open one. 'unused': E-mails never resolve an incident. 'any': An e-mail resolves an incident when at least one of `resolvedRules` matches. 'all': An e-mail resolves an incident when all of `resolvedRules` match.

resolvedRules.description: The conditions `resolvedRuleType` checks, with the same keys as `startedRules`. At least one is required when the type is 'any' or 'all'.

sms.description: Whether to send an SMS to the on-call person. Ignored while an escalation policy is set.

startedAlertIdField.description: How to extract the alert ID from the e-mail that starts an incident, with the same keys as `causeField`. Later e-mails acknowledge or resolve the open incident with the same alert ID. Required when `acknowledgedRuleType` or `resolvedRuleType` isn't 'unused'.

startedRuleType.description: When e-mails open an incident. Every value other than 'unused' needs at least one rule. When `startedAlertIdField` finds an alert ID that matches an open incident, the e-mail goes to that incident instead of opening a new one. 'unused': Every e-mail that doesn't acknowledge or resolve an incident opens one. 'any': An e-mail opens an incident when at least one of `startedRules` matches. 'all': An e-mail opens an incident when all of `startedRules` match.

startedRules.description: The conditions `startedRuleType` checks. At least one rule is required when the type is 'any' or 'all'.

titleField.description: Field that extracts the incident title, with the same keys as `causeField`.

A user, team or parent field accepts one `{label, value}` object, and a single-select or priority field the option's ID as a string. A number field accepts a number, and a date picker field an ISO 8601 time such as `2026-12-01T09:00:00Z`.

customWebhookTemplateAttributes.description: Custom request method, headers, body and basic authentication. Without it, an 'incident_change' or 'monitor_change' webhook sends the incident or monitor under 'data', with what happened in 'event', such as 'started' or 'created'. An 'on_call_change' webhook then sends the on-call calendar's 'message', 'emails', 'on_holiday_emails', 'change', 'calendar_id', 'calendar_name' and 'primary_calendar' under 'data'. 'v3': Renders `$METADATA.` as all the key's values joined by commas. `$METADATA_ARRAY` and `$METADATA..values` list each value with its type.

onIncidentAcknowledged.description: Whether to send the webhook when an incident is acknowledged. Only for an 'incident_change' webhook. Defaults to true.

onIncidentComment.description: Whether to send the webhook when a comment is added to an incident. The default body then also has a 'comment' object, whose 'attributes' hold the comment's 'content', 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'user_id' and 'user_email'. Only for an 'incident_change' webhook. Defaults to true.

onIncidentReopened.description: Whether to send the webhook when an incident is reopened. Only for an 'incident_change' webhook. Defaults to true.

onIncidentResolved.description: Whether to send the webhook when an incident is resolved. Only for an 'incident_change' webhook. Defaults to true.

onIncidentStarted.description: Whether to send the webhook when an incident starts. Only for an 'incident_change' webhook. Defaults to true.

triggerType.description: What triggers the webhook. Fixed once the integration is created. 'incident_change': Sends the webhook when an incident starts, is acknowledged, resolved or reopened, or gets a comment. 'on_call_change': Sends the webhook when the person on call changes, or when their holiday starts or ends during their shift. 'monitor_change': Sends the webhook when a monitor is created, updated, paused, unpaused or removed.

url.description: The URL the webhook is sent to. For an 'incident_change' webhook, it can use the `$INCIDENT_ID`, `$TEAM_ID` and `$METADATA` variables.

outputs.description: A collection of values returned by getOnCallRotation.

applyFrom.description: When this change applies, as **Apply changes from** in the web app. Shifts before it are kept. Leave it out to apply the change now.

applyFromTimezone.description: Time zone that `applyFrom` is read in when it has no UTC offset. Defaults to UTC.

effectiveTimezone.description: Time zone that `workingHours` actually use. It's `timezone` when set, else the schedule's default time zone, else `UTC`.

id.description: The ID of the on-call rotation to look up.

rotationInterval.description: Unit for `rotationLength`. Valid values: 'hour', 'day', 'week'.

rotationLength.description: Number of intervals each shift lasts, a whole number of at least '1'.

teamId.description: Team of the rotation's on-call schedule, such as 't123'. Defaults to the provider's `teamId`. Set it to look the object up in another team.

timezone.description: Time zone for `workingHours` and for handovers across daylight saving changes. A new rotation with `workingHours` defaults to UTC.

users.description: E-mail addresses of users in the rotation, in shift order. Each must be a responder in the schedule's team.

workingHours.description: The windows in which the rotation pages anyone, as up to 50 windows in local time. They are returned as `HH:MM`, sorted by day. A window that ends at or before its start runs overnight, and one with the same start and end covers the whole day. Without it, or with an empty list, the rotation pages around the clock.

inputs.description: A collection of arguments for invoking getStatusPage.

id.description: The ID of the status page to look up.

outputs.description: A collection of values returned by getStatusPage.

aggregateState.description: The page's overall status. 'operational': No resource on the page is down, degraded or in maintenance. 'degraded': A resource is degraded and none is down. 'downtime': A resource is down. 'maintenance': A resource is in maintenance and none is down or degraded.

announcementEmbedCss.description: Your own CSS for the announcement on the embeddable widget.

announcementEmbedLink.description: Link the announcement points to on the embeddable widget.

announcementEmbedVisible.description: Whether the embeddable widget shows the announcement.

automaticReports.description: Whether status page reports are created automatically for new incidents.

companyName.description: Company name shown on the page.

contactUrl.description: URL visitors can use to get in touch, such as a support page or a `mailto:` address like `mailto:support@example.com`.

createdAt.description: When the status page was created.

customCss.description: Custom CSS added to the page.

customDomain.description: A host name you own to serve the page from, such as `status.example.com`. Point its CNAME record to `statuspage.betteruptime.com`.

customJavascript.description: Custom JavaScript added to the page.

darkLogoRemoteUrl.description: The URL the dark mode logo was fetched from.

darkLogoUrl.description: The logo shown in dark mode. Responses return the URL of the stored logo.

deletionProtection.description: Whether destroying or replacing this status page is refused. Defaults to true. Set it to false and apply before you delete or replace it on purpose. It's kept in state and never sent to Better Stack.

design.description: Page design. 'v1': The classic design. 'v2': The modern design.

faviconRemoteUrl.description: The URL the favicon was fetched from.

faviconUrl.description: The icon browsers show in the page's tab, as the URL of the stored favicon. Only the 'v2' design shows it.

googleAnalyticsId.description: Your Google Analytics ID, such as `G-XXXXXXXX`. It must start with `G-`, `UA-` or `GTM-`.

hideFromSearchEngines.description: Whether to hide the page from search engines with a 'noindex' tag.

history.description: Number of days of history the page shows, from 7 to 365.

id.description: The ID of the status page to look up.

ipAllowlist.description: IP addresses or CIDR ranges allowed to view the page. Entries starting with `#` are comments.

layout.description: Header layout of the page. Only the 'v2' design uses it. Valid values: 'vertical', 'horizontal'.

logoRemoteUrl.description: The URL the light mode logo was fetched from.

logoUrl.description: The logo shown in light mode. Responses return the URL of the stored logo.

minIncidentLength.description: Shortest incident the page shows, in seconds. '0' shows every incident.

navigationLinks.description: Up to four links in the page's navigation, each with `text` and `href`. Only the 'v2' design shows them. An empty list removes them all.

organizationId.description: The ID of the organization the page belongs to, such as '123'. Get the ID from `organizationId` in [List teams](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/teams/list/).

password.description: Password visitors enter to view the page. Never returned. Setting a password also turns on `passwordEnabled`, unless `passwordEnabled` is set too. An empty password removes the password and turns protection off.

passwordEnabled.description: Whether visitors need a password to view the page. Off unless you turn it on or set `password`.

publicUrl.description: The address visitors open the page at. It is the `customDomain` when the page has one, otherwise the betterstack.com `subdomain`.

published.description: Whether the page is published and publicly visible. An unpublished page is a draft. Publishing a draft fails when the organization already has as many published status pages as its plan allows.

requireSso.description: Whether visitors must sign in with SSO to view the page. Needs SSO set up for your organization, and can't be on together with `passwordEnabled`.

sections.description: The page's sections and their resources, in display order. Setting it replaces the whole structure. Sections and resources are matched by `id`. Ones without an `id` are created. Ones left out are removed from the page. The monitors and other records behind them aren't affected. An attribute a resource leaves out keeps its value. Leave it out to keep the structure as it is. Only an update accepts it.

statusPageGroupId.description: The ID of the status page group the page belongs to. Get the ID via [List status page groups](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/list-all-status-page-groups/).

subdomain.description: Subdomain of the page's default address. It must be unique across Better Stack, up to 63 characters of letters, digits, dashes and underscores.

subscribable.description: Whether visitors can subscribe to updates.

theme.description: Color theme. Only the 'v2' design uses it. Valid values: 'light', 'dark', 'system'.

timezone.description: Time zone the page shows times in, as a Rails time zone name such as `Tokyo` or an IANA ID such as `Europe/Prague`. Returned as the Rails name.

treatNotMonitoredAsOperational.description: Whether the days a resource wasn't monitored show as operational in its history and count toward its uptime, instead of showing as not monitored.

updatedAt.description: When the status page was last updated.

whitelabeled.description: Whether to remove Better Stack branding from the page.

name.description: Group name.

organizationId.description: Organization the group belongs to, such as '123'. Required when you sign in with OAuth and can access more than one organization, otherwise the token's own organization. Not returned in responses.

sortIndex.description: Display order among the organization's status page groups. Lower values come first. Writes also accept it as 'position'.

inputs.description: A collection of arguments for invoking getTeam.

id.description: The ID of the team to look up.

outputs.description: A collection of values returned by getTeam.

deletionProtection.description: Whether destroying or replacing this team is refused. Defaults to true. Set it to false and apply before you delete or replace it on purpose. It's kept in state and never sent to Better Stack.

id.description: The ID of the team to look up.

incidentGroupingMetadataScope.description: Metadata keys whose values must match for incidents to be grouped. New teams start with `["Origin"]`. null groups the same way as `["Origin"]`.

incidentGroupingPeriod.description: Seconds within which a new incident is grouped with an earlier one that's still open, for example '300' for 5 minutes. '0' never groups incidents. From '0' to '2147483647', and new teams start at '300'.

logoRemoteUrl.description: The URL the team's logo was fetched from.

name.description: The team's name. It must be unique in the organization, ignoring letter case.

notifyAboutAllIncidentsInAGroup.description: Whether every incident in a group alerts, rather than only the first. New teams start at true.

onCallReminderEmail.description: Send on-call reminders by e-mail. New teams start at true.

onCallReminderLeadTime.description: Seconds before an on-call shift starts to remind the person, or '0' for no reminder. The other values are '3600', '21600', '43200', '86400', '172800' and '604800'. New teams start at '86400'.

onCallReminderPush.description: Send on-call reminders as push notifications. New teams start at true.

onCallReminderSms.description: Send on-call reminders by SMS. New teams start at false.

openedEmailsTrackingEnabled.description: Whether the incident timeline records when a team member opens the e-mail about a new incident. New teams start at true.

organizationId.description: ID of the organization the team belongs to.

reportingEnabled.description: Whether reporting is on, which unlocks the reports in Incidents. New teams start at false.

updatedAt.description: When the team was last updated.

inputs.description: A collection of arguments for invoking getTeamMember.

id.description: The ID of the team member to look up.

teamId.description: Team the membership is in, such as 't123'. Defaults to the provider's `teamId`. Set it to look the object up in another team.

outputs.description: A collection of values returned by getTeamMember.

createdAt.description: When the user account was created. Absent on a pending invitation.

deletionProtection.description: Whether destroying or replacing this team member is refused. Defaults to true. Set it to false and apply before you delete or replace it on purpose. It's kept in state and never sent to Better Stack.

email.description: E-mail address.

firstName.description: The member's first name, or null when they haven't set one. Absent on a pending invitation.

id.description: The ID of the team member to look up.

invitedAt.description: When the invitation was created. Present only on a pending invitation.

lastName.description: The member's last name, or null when they haven't set one. Absent on a pending invitation.

mobileAppPlatforms.description: The platforms the member's mobile apps receive push notifications on, 'ios' and 'android', or empty when none. Absent on a pending invitation.

role.description: The member's built-in role in this team. A user can have a different role in each team. null on an invitation to a custom role. With neither `role` nor `roleId`, an invitation gets the responder role. 'admin': Can access every feature in every team, including billing, organization settings and API tokens. The API never assigns it. 'billing_admin': Can manage subscriptions, invoices and payment settings for the whole organization, without access to operational features. 'team_lead': Can access monitors, incidents, on-call, status pages, telemetry and AI SRE, invite team members and change their roles. 'responder': Can access monitors, incidents, on-call, status pages, telemetry and AI SRE, and invite team members. 'member': Can access sources, Live tail, dashboards, error tracking, session replays and AI SRE, without monitors, incidents or on-call. 'custom': The member has a custom role. Assign one with `roleId` instead.

roleId.description: ID of the member's role, or of the role an invitation gives, custom roles included. Get the IDs via [List roles](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/roles/list/). When `role` is also given, both must name the same role.

teamId.description: Team the membership is in, such as 't123'. Defaults to the provider's `teamId`. Set it to look the object up in another team.
